name: Li Wenbin
current_role: Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer, Lee & Man Paper Manufacturing Ltd (HKEX: 2314)
profile: Li Wenbin (Lee Man Bun, MH JP; also known as Edmond Lee) is the younger son of Lee & Man founder Lee Wan Keung Patrick and brother of chairman Raymond Lee Man Chun. He has run Hong Kong-listed Lee & Man Paper, one of China's largest containerboard/tissue makers, as CEO since about 2013-14, and his family holds a large stake.
interesting_fact: Lee & Man Paper is one of Asia's largest packaging-paper producers, with mills across mainland China plus operations in Vietnam and Malaysia; the Lee family also controls sister firm Lee & Man Chemical.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a chemical engineer at the University of British Columbia, and was already an executive director and assistant general manager of the family paper company at age 26 (2005/06 annual report).
notes: Hurun lists him jointly with Ho Tsz Wan. No personal channels found; route via Lee & Man Paper head office (39/F Lee & Man Commercial Center, North Point, HK) / company secretary. UBC degree per MarketScreener profile.

name: Tung Ching Sai
current_role: Executive Director and CEO, Xinyi Glass Holdings (HKEX: 868); chairman of Xinyi Electric Storage; director at Xinyi Solar/Xinyi Energy
profile: Tung Ching Sai has been CEO of Hong Kong-listed Xinyi Glass, a maker of float, automotive and architectural glass whose customers include Ford, GM and VW, since 2004. He is the brother of vice-chairman Tung Ching Bor and brother-in-law of founder-chairman Lee Yin Yee; he also chairs the group's energy-storage arm.
interesting_fact: Beyond glass, he sits across the Xinyi group's clean-energy businesses (Xinyi Solar, Xinyi Energy) and chairs Xinyi Electric Storage, a natural fit for an energy-focused conversation.
deep_cut_fact: Xinyi Glass's own annual report styles him 'Tan Sri Datuk' Tung Ching Sai, i.e. he holds Malaysian honorific titles, unusual for a Hong Kong/mainland industrialist (Xinyi has major manufacturing in Malaysia).
notes: Low public profile; no personal channels found. Route via Xinyi Glass company secretary / IR in Hong Kong. Energy angle: Xinyi Solar and Xinyi Electric Storage. Malaysian manufacturing link stated as general context, not individually verified.

name: Wang Wenhui
current_role: Director and co-controlling shareholder, Guangzhou Ruoyuchen Technology (SZSE: 003010)
profile: Wang Wenhui (b. 1985) co-founded Guangzhou e-commerce services firm Ruoyuchen in 2011 with her husband, chairman/CEO Wang Yu; together they control roughly 43%. Ruoyuchen began as a cross-border/online store operator for international brands and has pivoted to its own brands such as LYCOCELLE (home care) and FineNutri (supplements). She has been a director since 2017.
interesting_fact: Ruoyuchen's growth has shifted from running Tmall/JD stores for foreign brands to building its own consumer brands (LYCOCELLE laundry care, FineNutri, NuiBay).
deep_cut_fact: Ruoyuchen started in May 2011 with registered capital of just RMB 100,000: she and Wang Yu each put in RMB 50,000. She served as the company's supervisor until 2015 and is also listed as its senior adviser on employee career development.
notes: Hurun lists her jointly with husband Wang Yu, who is the public face (chairman). Best route is via Ruoyuchen's board secretary / IR. Not on-theme for energy/data centers.

name: Chen Chenghui
current_role: Chairman, Kehua Data Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 002335), Xiamen; also chairs Kehua Digital Energy (Kehua Shuneng)
profile: Chen Chenghui (b. 1960, Pinghe, Fujian) is a PhD, professor-level electrical engineer who built Kehua (formerly Kehua Hengsheng) from a Zhangzhou instrument factory into a major maker of UPS power systems, data-center infrastructure, solar inverters and energy storage. He has been chairman since 2010 and holds ~17% of the company.
interesting_fact: Kehua is squarely in the podcast's lane: it supplies UPS/critical power and builds and operates data centers (IDC), and its Kehua Digital Energy arm sells PV inverters and battery storage systems.
deep_cut_fact: Before Kehua, he was deputy director of the Zhangzhou Kelong Electronic Instrument Factory (hence the 'Kelong' in some rich-list entries). He is a National Model Worker, May 1st Labour Medal winner and sat on the first expert committee of the China Power Supply Society.
notes: Highly relevant for energy/data-center podcast. Route via board secretary (Lin Tao) in Xiamen; company also runs overseas marketing that may handle English-language media.
